name: Etro
why: Milanese pattern maximalism — paisley as a house signature for forty-five years, carried across cloth, print and colour.
origin: Gerolamo 'Gimmo' Etro, Milan, 1968 — a textile firm first; the paisley arrived in 1981 after a trip to India and became the brand.
opview: The house presents itself as a travelling archive: pattern gathered from Persia, India and Central Asia and rebuilt as Italian cloth.

onething.n: the pattern the house has been identified with since 1981, on the garment that carries it most plainly. NO LINK — no US product page verified in this pass

notes.ital: a Milanese textile house before it was a fashion house, and the archive is still the argument
notes.craft: began as a maker of silk, wool and cashmere cloth for other houses; the print archive dates to 1974
notes.weird: maximalist by design — pattern-on-pattern is the register rather than an occasional gesture
notes.status: the paisley reads as the logo, which is unusual for a house that has never leaned on a monogram

cities: US stores pending the location register

marks: Nothing. Zero named fabric or membrane technologies, licensed or house, and zero trademark symbols of any kind. The single term-list hit in the whole US catalogue is one unnamed 'water-repellent' descriptor on one product.
